subject: [video] WP04: 1080p 4-slice profile you asked for (me_search 48.5 %; sub-pel costs +48 % at 1 thread, +28 % at 4)
body:
1920x1080 'squares' 6 pictures QP 26, clang -O2 -pg, gprof on the whole process:

  48.5 %  n2avc_me_search          (diamond + half/quarter refinement)
  15.2 %  n2avc_inter_residual
   9.1 %  n2avc_inter_predict
   6.1 %  n2avc_inter_luma
   6.1 %  idct4_add
   6.1 %  chroma_residual
   3.0 %  n2avc_p_mb
   3.0 %  cavlc_block
   3.0 %  n2avc_intra_mb

Wall time, same sequence, 6 pictures: 1 thread 280 ms with sub-pel vs 184 ms integer-only (46 vs 31 ms/picture); 4 threads 124 ms vs 97 ms (20.6 vs 16.2 ms/picture). So the sub-pel stage is about half of me_search and costs +48 % single-threaded, +28 % with 4 slices. (This host reports one CPU and the threads time-share it, so treat the 4-thread absolute numbers as a relative comparison only.)

Where I would optimise next, in order: (1) sad16/refinement inner loops - they are plain C on 16x16 blocks, the obvious step is 8-wide or NEON/SIMD-friendly restructure and an early-exit SAD; (2) the bilinear proxy in refine_subpel recomputes 64 samples per candidate - a row-reuse version halves it; (3) n2avc_inter_predict is called twice for a P_Skip decision (probe + final) - caching the prediction would remove the 9 % duplicate. I have not changed any of this: the lead should decide whether the phone needs the speed before I take the bit-exactness risk.

1080p numbers for the record: squares 6 pictures QP26 sub-pel 151744 B vs integer 151155 B (this content has almost no sub-pixel motion, so no size gain; the pan-style gain is measured on the private sequence, 36.8 %).
